steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
When you don't have time to read a long text like a notice, report or meeting pack, hand the summary to Claude.

Today you'll learn four new things.

  1. Say how long, and for whom
  2. Pull out just what you need
  3. Check dates and numbers against the original
  4. Keep it from making things up
  • Time: 15 minutes
  • You need: a computer where you've done Work 1 (moving files)

steps.title: Get the sample notice into Practice
steps.html:
It's an HR notice about '2027 working-hour changes'. It's fairly long.

⬇ Download the sample notice.txt

As in Work 1, drag notice.txt from Downloads into the Practice folder.

check.q: Is notice.txt in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If getting the file doesn't work
steps.html:
• If clicking shows the text on screen, save it there with Ctrl+S (⌘+S on a Mac) as notice.txt.
  • Moving works like 'Move it into the Practice folder' in Work 1. Right-click → Cut → Paste in Practice also works.

steps.title: Start with a new chat
steps.html: Claude app → Code tab → + New. Check the buttons under the typing box show Local · Practice · Manual.

check.q: Can you see Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the start screen looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder isn't Practice, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose it.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual.

steps.title: Ask for a 3-line summary
steps.html: Saying how long and for whom makes it far more useful than just "summarize".
steps.code: Summarize notice.txt in 3 lines for someone reading it for the first time

steps.title: If there's no summary or it's too long
steps.html:
• If it can't find the file, check notice.txt is inside the Practice folder.
  • Too long? Say "Shorter, one point per line."

steps.title: Pull out just what you need
steps.html: The same notice matters differently to different people. Tell it who you are.
steps.code: I'm a team lead. From this notice, list only what I need to do and by when

check.q: Did you get team-lead tasks like spreading out work-from-home days and submitting the team plan by the last Friday of each month?

steps.title: If unrelated things got mixed in
steps.html: Make the criteria clearer, e.g. "Split it into what applies to everyone and what applies only to team leads."

steps.title: Pull out dates and numbers and check them
steps.html:
The riskiest thing in a summary is wrong dates and numbers. Pull them out and check.

  1. Send the sentence below.
  2. Open notice.txt in the Practice folder (Notepad), press Ctrl+F (⌘+F on a Mac), find December 15, and compare it with the table.
steps.alt: A table of just the dates and numbers from the notice
steps.code: Pull out just the dates and numbers as a table, exactly as in the original

check.q: Did the application deadline (December 15) match the original?

steps.title: If it doesn't match the original
steps.html: That's exactly why you check. Say "Find the application deadline in the original again and quote the exact sentence." If it still differs, trust the original.

steps.title: Keep it from making things up
steps.html: AI sometimes answers with plausible-sounding inventions. Let's ask about something that isn't in the notice.
steps.code: Does this notice say anything about lunch-break changes? If it's not in the original, say so

check.q: Did it say it's not in the original?

steps.title: If it said yes
steps.html:
The notice says nothing about lunch breaks. The AI made it up. Asking "Which sentence in the original says that? Quote it" usually gets it to correct itself.

From now on, add "Don't include anything that isn't in the original" when you ask for summaries.

steps.title: Save it to a file
steps.html: The summary only lives in the chat. Saving it to a file makes it easy to share. Read the create-file permission card and click Allow.
steps.code: Save the 3-line summary, the team-lead tasks and the dates table to notice-summary.txt

check.q: Is there a notice-summary.txt in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If you don't see the file
steps.html:
• If you denied the card, send it again and allow it.
  • Close the folder window and open it again.

steps.title: Do the same with other documents
steps.html:
• PDF: attach it with + next to the typing box, or put it in Practice and say "Summarize X.pdf".
  • Word files: if it can't read one well, save it as PDF in Word or paste the text in.
  • Very long documents: split it up, e.g. "Just chapters 1 to 3 first", for better accuracy.
  • Contracts and legal documents: use the summary only as a guide; check the original and an expert before important decisions.
Before handing over company documents, check your company's AI usage rules.

steps.title: 🎉 Work practice 2 done! What you learned
steps.html:
Without reading the whole notice, you pulled out exactly what you needed.

Set the format"In 3 lines, for someone new to it"
Who you are"I'm a team lead. Only my tasks and deadlines"
Check facts"Just dates and numbers as a table" → compare with the original
No inventions"If it's not in the original, say so"

Remember

Summaries save time, but the responsibility is yours. Double-check important dates and numbers in the original.
